title: Flowise record-manager and memory nodes -- T1059 additionalConfig grants full TypeORM DataSource control, entities loads arbitrary JS
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69251, an elttam-disclosed
advisory affecting five Flowise nodes (MySQL/Postgres/SQLite Record
Manager, MySQL Agent Memory, and the shared `AgentMemory.ts`).

Each of these nodes lets the caller set arbitrary options for a
TypeORM `DataSource` through the `additionalConfig` node input, with
no restriction on which options are allowed. TypeORM's `DataSource`
options support `entities`, `subscribers`, and `migrations` --
filesystem paths whose contents TypeORM loads and executes as
JavaScript when the DataSource initializes. An authenticated user
uploads a file containing a reverse-shell one-liner
(`process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...)`) through
the ordinary File Loader, then sets a Record Manager node's
`additionalConfig.entities` to that uploaded file's path. The next
Upsert Vector Store operation initializes the DataSource, TypeORM
loads the "entity" file as code, and the reverse shell fires --
confirmed as root on the published Docker image.

Detection logic flags a Record Manager or Agent Memory node
configuration whose `additionalConfig` sets `entities`,
`subscribers`, or `migrations` to a path outside the node's own
managed schema directory -- the exact
attacker-controlled-DataSource-option class this advisory's
end-to-end reverse-shell reproduction exploits.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (elttam, via
a disclosed advisory citing all five affected node source files, the
TypeORM `entities`/`subscribers`/`migrations` code-loading mechanism
by name, and a fully reproduced reverse shell with `uid=0(root)`
confirmation), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
